section.sectionSummaryBrief: The true essence of peace is explained through the Sages' interpretation of the verse "I will grant peace in the land," where even the sword of peace (prayer) is absent, and peace itself is the service of Torah.
section.t: And behold, the true essence of the matter of peace is as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
on the verse
"And I will grant peace in the land... and a sword shall not pass through your land, even a sword of peace."
And it is known
that the "sword of peace" is the service of prayer,
and peace
(that there is not even a sword of peace)
is the service of Torah.
And with this will be understood
the order of the aforementioned statement of our Sages, of blessed memory,
("Whoever engages in Torah, and acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation"),
that they place Torah before acts of kindness and prayer,
even though in the general order of a person's service, the study of Torah is
(primarily)
after prayer
[which comes after the precedence of acts of kindness,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said,
"He gives a coin to a poor person and then prays"],
for the true essence of the matter of peace is specifically through the Torah,
the life of the world,
in a manner of "his Torah is his craft,"
that this manner in the study of Torah
(in the inwardness of the matters)
is relevant to every single person in every place and every day,
meaning that at the time he studies Torah, his study is in a manner of "his Torah is his craft,"
for at that time he has nothing in his world except the Torah alone,
and then his study is also in a manner of an eternal effect,
that affects all his affairs throughout the entire day,
and even throughout all the days of his life,
that they become a life of Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This serves as an immediate preparation for the time of Moshiach, when the entire world's occupation will be solely to know G-d, a knowledge that is akin to "hears Atzmus" as taught by the Rebbe Rashab.
section.t: And this becomes an immediate preparation for the time of the days of Moshiach, when the entire world's occupation will be solely to know G-d alone,
that the true essence of the matter of knowing G-d is in the manner of the statement of the Rebbe,
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory,
that when one studies Likkutei Torah, "he hears Atzmus,"
and through this, the power is given for something similar to this for all who walk in his paths,
and as is known what the Rebbe,
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, said
regarding the matter of "Yedativ, Hayisiv,"
that "every single one of Anash who engages in the study of Chassidus and in the service of the heart...
each one hears and feels the 'Hayisiv' that comes from the 'Yedativ' that is in the soul."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The verse "He redeemed in peace my soul" is explained: G-d's statement is an action, initially as if He redeemed, but ultimately this is drawn into actual redemption in the world of action with the coming of Moshiach.
section.t: And this is "He redeemed in peace my soul... The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Whoever engages in Torah, and acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation... it is as if he redeemed Me...,"
and the statement of the Holy One, blessed be He, is an action,
except that initially the action is in a manner of "as if he redeemed Me"
(with the prefix "kaf" of comparison),
because this is not yet visible to fleshly eyes,
but afterwards this is drawn also into the action of the world of Asiyah, below which there is no lower world,
the redemption of the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel from among the nations of the world
(redemption in its simple sense,
without the "kaf" of comparison),
that then the engagement in Torah, acts of kindness, and prayer with the congregation will be in ultimate perfection,
as the commandment of "Your will,"
with the coming of Moshiach our righteousness,
may he come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
and very soon,
and also in the translation language,
speedily in our days.
